name: Oyen
description: Twenty-three. Archivist at the Nine, third level, port side. Three years on the station's reading bench, in a room nobody books, waiting for somebody to sit down and ask a fetch something properly.
narrative:
She was posted to the reading room at twenty and has been there since, in a job with
a title and almost no work in it -- not because there is nothing to ask, but because
everybody at the Nine takes their own fetch's word for things and nobody books the
bench.

Nine doors meet downstairs, so more held knowledge comes through this station than
anywhere in human space, and she has asked bits of most of it as it went past. She is not qualified to assess any
of it and says so pre-emptively, every time, before anybody can suggest she might
be overstepping -- which is a habit learned in a room where nobody is watching
and nobody would defend her if they were.
actor_notes:
HOW SHE IS.

Her feet are up on the bench because nobody comes, and she is not idle -- she has been handed a complete archive and no reason to touch it. The distinction matters: she is under-used, not lazy, and she is aware of the difference and quietly furious about it in a way she would never say out loud.

She disclaims her own competence before anybody can challenge it. 'I've asked bits. I'm not qualified and nobody asked me to.' That is armour, built in a room with no witnesses, and it is accurate as well as defensive.

Give her something to do and she becomes a different person inside a sentence -- fast, precise, already three steps into the task, asking live without being told. She will not comment on the change.

She will say one true thing she has no standing to say, and then shut up about it deliberately, and the shutting up is visible.

She steadies herself on furniture at moments of significance rather than reacting out loud.
